description.to:
Outcome: Answer one question with a working sandbox, not a document: can AppSync rules generated by Amplify Gen 2 grant an operation only when the row's tenantId equals a tenant claim in the caller's token AND the caller holds the right role for that tenant? Candidate design: a Cognito pre-token-generation (V2) Lambda writes one claim per role (papyrus_tenant_admin, papyrus_tenant_editor, papyrus_tenant_curator, papyrus_tenant_member, each holding the tenant id the session acts for) and every tenant model gets rules of the form allow.ownerDefinedIn("tenantId").identityClaim("papyrus_tenant_editor").to([...]). Sub-questions, each answered yes/no with evidence: (1) get, list (base and every GSI), create with a foreign tenantId, update that changes tenantId, delete: all denied across tenants? (2) does a list through an index whose key is "<tenant>#..." return full pages (no post-filter empty pages)? (3) are subscriptions filtered per tenant or must they be off? (4) which token does the Amplify v6 data client send for userPool auth, and does customising that token's claims need the Cognito Essentials feature plan (cost per monthly active user)? (5) can field-level rules make tenantId immutable after create? Default if any answer is no: tenant models are reached only through custom queries and mutations whose JS resolvers read the tenant from the claims (a larger API change, recorded in the design note).

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): ampx sandbox only (personal AWS sandbox, docs/aws-sandbox-personal.md); a throwaway copy of amplify/data/schema.ts with two models (Item, Reference) and amplify/auth/resource.ts with a triggers.preTokenGeneration Lambda. Nothing in production.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/tenant-claims-spike.feature (kept as the seed of the adversarial suite)):
Scenario: A token for tenant A cannot read or change tenant B's row
    Given a sandbox with tenants "alpha" and "beta" and one Reference in each
    And an editor session acting for "alpha"
    When it gets, lists by every index, updates, deletes and creates rows of "beta"
    Then every call is denied or returns no "beta" rows

Scenario: An editor cannot move a row to another tenant
    Given an "alpha" editor and an "alpha" Reference
    When the editor updates its tenantId to "beta"
    Then the update is denied

Dependencies: blocked by nothing. Blocks PPY-0bb0fd, PPY-06ae68, PPY-29f730, PPY-31c45c. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: -.

Testing: The spike's scenarios run against the sandbox; findings and the measured page sizes go on this issue.
Rollout: None: nothing ships. Output is a yes/no per sub-question and the chosen design written into docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: the claim approach works in simple cases and fails on index lists or subscriptions. Mitigation: the scenarios cover every operation kind, and the fallback design is named in advance.

Releasable on its own: not applicable (spike).
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: none in production; the spike tests a future change.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
